provider: Copernicus Programme data distributed through ESA’s Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (CDSE) as a Copernicus Contributing Mission product. Based on WorldDEM from the TanDEM-X mission; official attribution credits DLR e.V. and Airbus Defence and Space GmbH.
exact_product_name_and_version: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, DGED native product: COP-DEM_GLO-30-DGED. The latest release listed on the official collection page is 2024_1 (July 2024); the page lists releases 2019_1 through 2024_1. Product handbook cited is Issue 5.0. Do not confuse this native tile product with another DEM.
variables_and_units: One elevation/height raster band; vertical units are metres. For native DGED, vertical reference is EGM2008 (EPSG:3855). Source page lists 32-bit floating point for DGED. This is a DSM, not a bare-earth DTM.
spatial_resolution: Nominal 30 m; official grid spacing is 1.0 arc-second in latitude for GLO-30 DGED. Native DGED/DTED tiles are 1° × 1° latitude/longitude.
temporal_coverage: TanDEM-X acquisition period: 2011–2015. Earlier elevation models were used locally to fill data gaps; the exact source epoch for each filled pixel is not specified on cited page. The product is static, not a time series.
coordinate_reference_system: Native DGED horizontal CRS: WGS84-G1150, EPSG:4326 (geographic coordinates); vertical CRS: EGM2008, EPSG:3855. Elevation vertical unit: metres.
download_method: Use Copernicus Browser or CDSE CCM OData/S3; query only 1° tiles intersecting site AOIs and clip locally.
authentication_requirements: Registered CDSE account; OData uses OAuth token, S3 requires generated credentials. Native GLO-30 is listed as free/open subject to CCM terms.
license_or_attribution: Official collection page says worldwide GLO-30 is available with a free license; the official 2025 CCM license document names COP-DEM-GLO-30-F as Global 30m Full, Free & Open. For public communication/distribution, use: ‘© DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved’. If adapted or modified, the page specifies: ‘produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved’. Follow the license terms for the selected instance/release.
availability_status: Worldwide land-surface coverage (~149 million km²); the official page describes GLO-30 as global. This includes the land locations of Vredefort (South Africa), Sudbury and Manicouagan (Canada); those sites are not individually named in the cited page. Available native formats include DGED and DTED; the official collection page lists release 2024_1 as the latest listed release.
expected_processing_effort: Low-to-moderate for three site subsets: specify a separate EPSG:4326 point/buffer or polygon AOI per site; query the CCM catalogue for COP-DEM_GLO-30-DGED / SAR_DGE_30 products intersecting each AOI; use the returned product IDs/S3 paths to download only intersecting 1° tiles via OData or S3; then mosaic as needed and clip to the AOI in GIS/GDAL. Keep all sites on the same release. Volume depends on buffer/area and number of intersecting tiles; no fixed size is specified on cited pages.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: Digital Surface Model (DSM): depicts the top-reflective Earth surface, including buildings, infrastructure and vegetation. It is not a bare-earth DTM. The official collection page distinguishes a DTM as terrain with buildings, infrastructure and vegetation removed.
limitations: ‘Global coverage’ is stated as a land-surface area (~149 million km²), not a continuous bathymetric surface; ocean pixels are not bare-earth elevations. GLO-30 is locally infilled from other DEM sources, so acquisition epoch and source can vary. The official page does not explicitly enumerate Vredefort, Sudbury or Manicouagan; their inclusion follows from the stated worldwide land coverage. Confirm exact release and access eligibility in the CDSE catalogue/account before bulk download.
source_basis: PHASE1_PLANNED_CATALOG_PRESERVED_NOT_PROOF_OF_ACQUISITION

provider: Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S), implemented by ECMWF; ERA5-Land is produced by replaying the land component of ECMWF ERA5.
exact_product_name_and_version: The official CDS pages identify the products by the two dataset short names above, but do not specify a numeric dataset release/version ('not specified on cited page'). ECMWF documentation distinguishes consolidated ERA5-Land (GRIB expver=0001) from preliminary near-real-time ERA5-Land-T (expver=0005). The land model uses IFS cycle CY45R1; that is the model version, not a separately stated dataset release number.
variables_and_units: CDS variable names and listed units: 2m_temperature, 2m_dewpoint_temperature (K; derive relative humidity from temperature and dewpoint via the saturation-vapour-pressure ratio; RH is not listed as a direct ERA5-Land variable); total_precipitation (m, accumulated liquid and frozen precipitation); 10m_u_component_of_wind and 10m_v_component_of_wind (m s-1; derive speed/direction from components); surface_pressure (Pa; included as an ERA5 forcing field); snow_depth (m), snow_depth_water_equivalent (m of water equivalent), snowfall (m of water equivalent), snow_cover (%); skin_temperature (K); surface_solar_radiation_downwards (J m-2). For hourly forecast accumulations, precipitation/radiation are accumulated from 00 UTC to the forecast step; hourly precipitation increments generally require differencing successive cumulative fields, with care at 00 UTC (previous 24-hour accumulation). Monthly product is monthly means of daily means; accumulated hydrological variables are expressed per day (e.g. precipitation in m/day), and accumulated radiation per day (J m-2/day). The CDS main-variable table gives base units; the ECMWF accumulation documentation specifies these monthly per-day conventions.
spatial_resolution: Global land-surface fields (oceans masked in ECMWF documentation). CDS distribution is a regular latitude-longitude grid at 0.1° x 0.1° (approximately 9 km); native HRES grid is reduced Gaussian TCo1279, approximately 9 km/~0.08°. The CDS product is regridded from native grid.
temporal_coverage: January 1950 to present; hourly product temporal resolution is hourly and is updated daily. Monthly product is monthly and updated with approximately 2–3 months' delay. ECMWF describes near-real-time ERA5-Land-T daily updates at about 5 days behind real time, with consolidated final ERA5-Land replacing provisional data about two months later. Actual latest date therefore varies by stream and update status.
coordinate_reference_system: CDS projection: regular latitude-longitude. ECMWF documentation states horizontal reference to the WGS84 ellipsoid; vertical reference over land is EGM96 geoid (over ocean, mean sea level approximated as coincident with geoid). EPSG identifier: not specified on cited page.
download_method: Use the CDS web form or CDS API for selected variables, dates and AOI; download GRIB/NetCDF.
authentication_requirements: CDS account and personal access token; manually accept the dataset Terms of Use.
license_or_attribution: Copernicus Products licence: free of charge, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free and perpetual, subject to its terms. Clear and visible attribution to the Copernicus programme/Copernicus Climate Change Service is required; adapted products need an appropriate 'Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information [Year]' notice, and publications/distributions must state that neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for subsequent use. ERA5-Land documentation additionally says cite the CDS catalogue entry and attribute the product. Confirm any dataset-specific terms at download time.
availability_status: Publicly available via the two official CDS records linked above. Hourly coverage begins January 1950 and continues to present with daily updates; final consolidated records lag near-real-time data by roughly 2–3 months. Monthly aggregated record begins January 1950, with updates delayed about 2–3 months. CDS access is on its regular 0.1° lat-lon grid; ECMWF documentation says native-grid MARS retrieval is available to ECMWF member states.
expected_processing_effort: Low for selecting and downloading a variable/time subset; the monthly product is already aggregated. Moderate for analysis requiring RH or wind speed/direction derivation, temperature-unit conversion, conversion of monthly accumulated quantities from per-day totals to mean fluxes, or de-accumulation of hourly forecast accumulations. Large global, multidecade hourly requests may be substantial; request only needed variables, dates and region.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: This is a model-based reanalysis, not a direct gridded observation product. ERA5-Land runs the H-TESSEL land-surface model forced by ERA5 meteorology; observations are not directly assimilated into the ERA5-Land land simulation, but indirectly influence it through ERA5 atmospheric forcing, which assimilates observations. Input temperature, humidity and pressure receive lapse-rate correction for the finer grid. Uncertainty grows further back in time as fewer observations support atmospheric forcing; ECMWF says ERA5 uncertainty fields can be used alongside ERA5-Land fields.
limitations: Estimates have model and forcing uncertainty and are not station observations. The dataset documentation says ERA5-Land has one high-resolution realization; uncertainty information is from the lower-resolution ERA5 ensemble. CDS data are regridded rather than native-grid values. Hourly total precipitation and radiation are forecast accumulations, not automatically independent one-hour increments; monthly accumulated values have per-day conventions. Known issue: snow depths of 10 m or greater indicate glacier/ice areas where snow depth is not well known; forecast parameters are missing at 1950-01-01 00 UTC. Product-version caveat: no numeric release identifier is stated on cited product pages.
source_basis: PHASE1_PLANNED_CATALOG_PRESERVED_NOT_PROOF_OF_ACQUISITION

provider: NASA EOSDIS Land Processes Distributed Active Archive Center (LP DAAC; archived/distributed through NASA Earthdata Cloud/LP DAAC).
exact_product_name_and_version: MODIS/Terra Land Surface Temperature/Emissivity Daily L3 Global 1 km SIN Grid, MOD11A1 Version 6.1; collection/version identifier 061 (CMR collection C1748058432-LPCLOUD).
variables_and_units: Day LST: LST_Day_1km, Kelvin; night LST: LST_Night_1km, Kelvin. NASA catalog gives a scale factor of 0.02 (stored integer values are scaled to Kelvin); product also contains QC, view-time/angle, emissivity, and clear-sky coverage layers.
spatial_resolution: Nominal 1 km; each MODIS tile is 1,200 × 1,200 cells. The official MOD11 guide specifies the grid spacing as 0.928 km × 0.928 km.
temporal_coverage: Daily; NASA CMR collection record starts 2000-02-24 (UTC). The record has no time_end, and the cited NASA catalog pages do not specify an end/latest granule date.
coordinate_reference_system: MODIS Sinusoidal (SIN) tiled grid. AppEEARS lists MODIS Sinusoidal as +proj=sinu +lon_0=0 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +R=6371007.181 +units=m +no_defs; its EPSG field is blank (no EPSG code specified there).
download_method: NASA Earthdata Search/LAADS for granules; AppEEARS area/point API for product/layer subsets.
authentication_requirements: NASA Earthdata Login required for downloads/API.
license_or_attribution: NASA Earthdata states the dataset is openly shared without restriction under EOSDIS Data Use and Citation Guidance; a separate named license is not specified on the cited product page. Attribute NASA LP DAAC and cite the product DOI https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MOD11A1.061.
availability_status: Daily HDF-EOS granules (file format HDF/HDF-EOS) are distributed by NASA LP DAAC; access is through the official NASA Earthdata Search/LAADS archive or AppEEARS for subsets. Collection metadata records availability from 2000-02-24 and no fixed end date.
expected_processing_effort: Moderate: select date/tile or submit a subset request, read the HDF-EOS SDS layers, apply the 0.02 scale factor to LST values, and interpret QC/clear-sky flags. Reprojection is optional if working in the native SIN grid.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: Satellite-derived land-surface temperature retrieved from Terra MODIS observations under clear-sky conditions; it is not a direct near-surface air-temperature measurement.
limitations: Cloud/clear-sky screening limits valid observations; NASA notes that above 30° latitude multiple qualifying clear-sky observations may be averaged. Land surface temperature represents the observed surface (for example soil, vegetation, snow, or built surfaces) and is not the near-surface air temperature reported in weather observations. The catalog does not state a collection end date.
source_basis: PHASE1_PLANNED_CATALOG_PRESERVED_NOT_PROOF_OF_ACQUISITION

provider: European Space Agency (ESA) WorldCover project; developed by the WorldCover consortium led by VITO Remote Sensing with partners.
exact_product_name_and_version: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200 (product reference year 2021; algorithm/product version v200; released October 2022).
variables_and_units: Map: single-byte categorical land-cover codes, no physical units: 10 Tree cover; 20 Shrubland; 30 Grassland; 40 Cropland; 50 Built-up; 60 Bare / sparse vegetation; 70 Snow and Ice; 80 Permanent water bodies; 90 Herbaceous wetland; 95 Mangroves; 100 Moss and lichen. Classes follow the FAO/UN Land Cover Classification System. InputQuality: three-band UINT16 GeoTIFF; band 1 = number of Sentinel-1 GAMMA0 observations used; band 2 = number of Sentinel-2 L2A observations used; band 3 = percentage (0–100) of invalid S2 observations discarded after cloud/cloud-shadow filtering. No scaling or offset is applied.
spatial_resolution: Map layer grid spacing is 1°/12000, approximately 10 m at the equator (not constant ground distance by latitude). InputQuality layer is 1/2000°, approximately 60 m at the equator. Delivered in 3° × 3° tiles as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs.
temporal_coverage: Annual thematic map for 1 January–31 December 2021; Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 observations covering the reference year are used. This is an annual product, not a dated single observation. Product coverage is land observed by Sentinel-2 in 2021, except Antarctica; northern limit 82.75°N.
coordinate_reference_system: Regular latitude/longitude grid, EPSG:4326, WGS 1984 ellipsoid. Tiles are geographic 3° × 3° blocks.
download_method: Public AWS S3 regional tiles or ESA viewer/Zenodo macrotiles; download only intersecting tiles.
authentication_requirements: AWS public map layer needs no AWS credentials; viewer/Terrascope routes require registration.
license_or_attribution: Free of charge and without restriction of use under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). ESA map-layer attribution: `© ESA WorldCover project 2021 / Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021) processed by ESA WorldCover consortium`. For publication cite Zanaga et al. (2022), ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200, DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7254221.
availability_status: ESA's product page identifies WorldCover 2021 v200 as an available product; its linked Zenodo record is the exact archived release. The official AWS Open Data Registry documents public S3 access with no AWS account required. Live bucket listing returned HTTP 200 and current objects under v200/2021/map/ at verification time.
expected_processing_effort: Product is preprocessed as COGs; no classification processing is needed to use the map. Global delivery comprises 2,651 tiles; the Map layer is approximately 117 GB. A regional subset requires identifying/downloading intersecting 3° tiles (or using viewer polygon/AOI ZIP); mosaicking/clipping may be needed for a seamless region. InputQuality is separate and is not in the public AWS map route.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: Derived annual classification, not a raw EO observation or direct pixel measurement. ESA's v200 manual describes preprocessing Sentinel-1 GRD Gamma0 and Sentinel-2 L2A time series, extracting annual features, training gradient-boosting decision-tree CatBoost models (combined, L2A-only, and GAMMA0-only scenarios), predicting labels/class probabilities, and combining scenarios with expert rules. Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 reference-year data are used.
limitations: ESA reports overall accuracy of 76.7% for v200 (see Product Validation Report V2.0; this is not a guarantee of per-pixel correctness). The manual's non-exhaustive v200 limitations include residual cloud artefacts under persistent cloud cover; visible Sentinel-2 orbit/block borders where class confusion and differing observation/input signal affect inference; glacier ablation zones and mountain shadows sometimes misclassified as water; and confusion between irrigated agriculture and herbaceous wetland. Coverage excludes Antarctica and is limited northward to 82.75°N. ESA cautions that differences from 2020 v100 combine real land-cover change with algorithm changes; most map changes between years are attributed to algorithm changes. The v200 manual's temporal section appears to contain a year typo ('WorldCover 2020 v200'); the product filename, manual naming convention, archive record, and ESA page consistently identify this v200 map as 2021.
source_basis: PHASE1_PLANNED_CATALOG_PRESERVED_NOT_PROOF_OF_ACQUISITION

exact_product_name_and_version: SoilGrids250m version 2.0 (SoilGrids 2.0). ISRIC's FAQ explicitly says it refers to SoilGrids250m version 2.0.
variables_and_units: The official layers table lists: bdod bulk density (stored cg/cm³; divide by 100 for kg/dm³); cec CEC buffered at pH 7 (mmol(c)/kg; ÷10 = cmol(c)/kg); cfvo coarse fragments (cm³/dm³, vol‰; ÷10 = cm³/100 cm³, vol%); clay, sand, silt (g/kg; ÷10 = g/100 g, %); nitrogen (cg/kg; ÷100 = g/kg); ocd organic-carbon density (hg/m³; ÷10 = kg/m³); ocs organic-carbon stock (t/ha; ÷10 = kg/m²); soc organic-carbon content (dg/kg; ÷10 = g/kg); phh2o pH in water (pH×10; ÷10 for pH); and wv0010, wv003, wv1500 volumetric water content at 10, 33, and 1500 kPa, respectively (stored 10⁻³ cm³/cm³; ÷10 = 10⁻² cm³/cm³, %). Integer storage and the conversion factors are stated by ISRIC. Standard intervals are 0–5, 5–15, 15–30, 30–60, 60–100, and 100–200 cm; organic-carbon stock is specifically topsoil 0–30 cm, with subsoil stocks described as in development. Note: the ISRIC layer table calls 33-kPa water content `wv003`, while the REST OpenAPI query defaults call it `wv0033`; preserve this discrepancy when selecting the API property code.
spatial_resolution: 250 m spatial resolution (250-m grid/cell, as described by ISRIC).
temporal_coverage: A spatial prediction product, not a dated time series; temporal coverage/date of the map layers is not specified on cited product pages. The SoilGrids 2.0 paper reports a 2020 production run and 2021 publication; its covariates include 2001–2015 averages for climatic variables and vegetation indices, which is not a stated temporal coverage for the soil maps.
coordinate_reference_system: ISRIC's WCS example specifies EPSG:152160 as both SUBSETTINGCRS and OUTPUTCRS; the 2021 SoilGrids 2.0 paper identifies the common projection as Goode's Homolosine on the WGS84 datum. WCS permits specifying subset and output CRS, so this example should not be read as proof that every format/default uses only this CRS.
download_method: WCS GetCoverage for spatial raster subsets; WebDAV for complete global VRT/GeoTIFF tiles; REST point service is documented but currently paused.
authentication_requirements: WCS/WebDAV auth is not specified on cited pages; REST API operational status is paused and authentication requirements are not specified.
license_or_attribution: Publicly available under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0), per ISRIC. ISRIC requests proper reference to the data provider and acknowledgements; the product FAQ cites Poggio et al. (2021), “SoilGrids 2.0: producing soil information for the globe with quantified spatial uncertainty,” SOIL 7, 217–240, DOI 10.5194/soil-7-217-2021. See ISRIC Data and Software Policy for data-use/citation terms.
availability_status: ISRIC's documentation identifies WMS, WCS, and WebDAV as access routes; WCS is documented for spatial subsets and WebDAV for complete global maps. The REST API is currently reported by ISRIC as temporarily paused, without an estimated restoration timeline. Current operational status of WCS/WebDAV is not specified on cited page.
expected_processing_effort: Precomputed model predictions; users need not train the mapping model. For raster subsets, select a coverage and supply spatial bounds, CRS, and output format to WCS; full-map access is through WebDAV/VRT and GeoTIFF tiles. Point extraction is offered in the REST API specification, but that service is currently paused. Further processing requirements are not specified on cited page.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: These are machine-learning spatial predictions, not direct measurements at each map cell. ISRIC describes models calibrated using global soil-profile observations from WoSIS and environmental covariates; the 2.0 documentation reports over 230,000 profile observations. Prediction uncertainty is provided through quantiles, including the 5th and 95th percentiles (a 90% prediction interval), mean, and median.
limitations: Applies to terrestrial Earth soil only; this is not lunar or Martian regolith data. The source paper defines the mapped soil concept as up to 2 m of unconsolidated material at Earth's surface in contact with the atmosphere, excluding subaqueous and tidally exposed soils and material deeper than 2 m. The product's land mask excludes urban, inland-water, glacier, and bare-surface classes; no estimate is provided for permanent ice. ISRIC reports model variation explained of about 30%–70%, uneven profile coverage (notably in some high-latitude, desert, coastal, and Central Asian areas), and lower-than-expected values for some organic-soil carbon stocks under investigation. Maps follow a rolling-release approach and may be updated.
source_basis: PHASE1_PLANNED_CATALOG_PRESERVED_NOT_PROOF_OF_ACQUISITION

provider: LOLA Science Team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; archived/distributed by NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Geosciences Node and the LOLA Data Node
exact_product_name_and_version: PDS3 dataset version V1.0 (LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0; DOI 10.17189/1520642). The PDS4 migrated bundle is urn:nasa:pds:lro_lola_rdr, version 1.0. The 1024-pixel/degree LDEM is described by the PDS dataset profile as preliminary and sparse. Dataset version is not the same as a per-grid acquisition epoch; GDRs are cumulative/reprocessed products.
variables_and_units: LDEM is gridded elevation/shape relative to a reference sphere; labeled integer values convert to HEIGHT (elevation) in meters as DN × SCALING_FACTOR. Planetary radius in meters is DN × SCALING_FACTOR + OFFSET, where OFFSET is the reference-sphere radius. The archive SIS specifies 16-bit integers scaled by 0.5 m for the standard binary elevation data, relative to datum (±16 km dynamic range); consult each product label for its scale/offset. The 2014 USGS 118 m GeoTIFF instance separately specifies scaler 0.5, offset 0, with reference radius 1,737.4 km. The dataset also includes sample density, albedo, slope, roughness, geoid height and 1064-nm surface reflectance. Slope/roughness output units are not specified on cited product-help pages.
spatial_resolution: Global standard equirectangular/simple-cylindrical LDEMs: LDEM_4 = 4 pixels/degree, 7.5808 km latitude pixel size; LDEM_16 = 16 ppd, 1.895 km; LDEM_64 = 64 ppd, 0.4738 km; LDEM_128 = 128 ppd, 0.2369 km; LDEM_256 = 256 ppd, 118.45 m; LDEM_512 = 512 ppd, 59.225 m; LDEM_1024 = 1024 ppd, 29.612 m. These are official table values (linear pixel dimensions are latitude spacing; longitude spacing is angularly equal and ground distance varies with latitude). LDEM_256 onward are tiled. The 1024 ppd map is preliminary/sparse per the PDS profile. Separate polar stereographic products, not global grids, are LDEM_45S_100M, LDEM_60S_60M, LDEM_75S_30M, LDEM_80S_20M, LDEM_85S_10M and LDEM_87S_5M for north/south coverage as described by the product page.
temporal_coverage: The PDS dataset profile gives observation span 2009-07-13T05:33:17.246Z through 2015-04-16T03:22:08.887Z (dataset release date 2015-12-15). These dates describe the archived GDR dataset profile, not a guarantee that every grid pixel has observations across the entire interval. Separately, the USGS March 2014 LDEM_256/118 m GeoTIFF page says its input measurements span July 2009–July 2013.
coordinate_reference_system: Global standard products use equirectangular (simple/equidistant cylindrical) projection. PDS Archive SIS specifies 0–360° longitude for binary IMG products; global JP2 uses projection-center longitude 0° following GIS practice, unlike the IMG 0–360 convention. The USGS 118 m GeoTIFF metadata identifies the Mean Earth/polar-axis (ME) coordinate system, planetocentric latitude, positive-east longitude, with longitude domain −180° to +180°. The PDS product help identifies LDEM_64_PA as a distinct product in the dynamically defined Principal Axis frame. Reference sphere/radius is 1,737,400 m for standard elevation products. Check the individual label because frame and longitude encoding differ by product/format.
download_method: Use PDS Geosciences Node/ODE or LOLA Data Node; choose explicit LDEM product and retain label.
authentication_requirements: No login is indicated for public PDS data access; verify product labels and coverage.
license_or_attribution: PDS Geosciences FAQ states PDS datasets are public domain and free to download; it recommends appropriate citation for published use. PDS dataset DOI: https://doi.org/10.17189/1520642. PDS profile citation names G.A. Neumann and dataset LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0; the USGS 118 m item credits the LOLA Science Team and says “Please cite authors.” No separate license text for individual GDR files is specified on the cited product pages.
availability_status: PDS dataset profile links Geosciences Web Service, Geosciences Online Archives and Lunar Orbital Data Explorer. PDS Geosciences LRO/LOLA landing page notes the LOLA Science Team Data Node is updated more frequently than PDS deliveries and directs users seeking the latest data to ODE. Product files may be IMG with detached PDS labels, floating-point IMG, or lossless JP2; global higher-resolution products are tiled. Official entry points: https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/missions/lro/lola.htm and https://ode.rsl.wustl.edu/moon/.
expected_processing_effort: Slope and roughness ancillary grids are already included in the GDR family, so using them is low effort after applying each label's scale/offset. Official GDRDSM documentation says bidirectional slope is calculated by fitting a plane to three successive laser shots, requiring n=5–15 profile returns; baseline varies about 30–120 m with orbital velocity, detection probability and spacecraft altitude. GDRDRM roughness is the per-pixel average residual standard deviation of altitudes from three successive laser shots after fitting a plane to n=5–15 profile returns, with the same stated 30–120 m variable baseline. The global ancillary products identified on those pages are LDSM_16 and LDRM_16. Their output units are not specified on those cited pages. Recomputing terrain derivatives from an LDEM instead requires choosing a method and scale; it will not automatically reproduce these instrument-profile-derived ancillary measures.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: Observed-altimetry-derived global shape/elevation products, not modeled substitutes: GDRDEM pages characterize pixels as binned and interpolated LOLA altimetric measurements on a uniform grid, with each pixel representing a mean at the cell center. Ancillary slope/roughness products are derived from LOLA shot profiles. Interpolated cells may not represent direct laser returns.
limitations: The exact product identifier is the GDR V1.0 dataset; 1024 ppd is explicitly preliminary and sparse. Higher-resolution global grids are tiled, and polar stereographic products are regional, not global. PDS profile coverage ends 2015-04-16 although LOLA/mission data acquisition continued; use the node/ODE for current releases where available. The USGS 2014 118 m map documents gaps between tracks commonly 1–2 km and locally up to 4 km near the equator, filled by interpolation. Scale, frame, longitude encoding and available coverage must be checked in each file label; the global IMG and JP2 longitude conventions differ. Exact slope/roughness units are not specified on the cited help pages.
source_basis: PHASE1_PLANNED_CATALOG_PRESERVED_NOT_PROOF_OF_ACQUISITION

provider: Diviner Science Team, University of California, Los Angeles; archived by NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Geosciences Node.
exact_product_name_and_version: PDS3 dataset ID/version: LRO-L-DLRE-5-GDR-V1.0. The migrated PDS4 archive is bundle urn:nasa:pds:lro_diviner_derived1::5.0 (DOI 10.17189/wj0s-w188); its GDR Level 2 data collection is urn:nasa:pds:lro_diviner_derived1:data_derived_gdr_level2::1.0. These are archive/container identifiers, not a replacement product version.
variables_and_units: Level 2 (GDR_L2): averaged solar reflectance (VB1/VB2), brightness temperatures TB3–TB9, local time (LTIM), and Julian Date (JD); AVG, error (ERR), and count (CNT) products; day and night splits are local time 06:00–18:00 and 18:00–06:00. The official GDR_L2 summary does not state the output units for these fields ('not specified on cited page'); it says thermal values outside 10–450 K are screened. Level 3 (GDR_L3): CF/NEN_CF, rock abundance (RA; ratio 0–1), soil temperature (ST; K), normalized soil temperature (STN; K), RMS fitting error, and bolometric temperature (TBOL). L3 soil temperature is explicitly reported in Kelvin; units for CF, RMS and TBOL are not specified on cited pages.
spatial_resolution: L2 cylindrical global maps: 128 ppd master grid plus 64, 16, 4 and 1 ppd. Polar stereographic: 126.347 ppd, corresponding to 240 m/pixel, to ±75° latitude. L3 thermal/rock maps: simple cylindrical, 32 ppd, latitude extent −60° to +60° (archive description notes some rock/soil products extended to ±80°).
temporal_coverage: Dataset profile: 2009-07-05T12:00:00Z to 2016-10-23T09:00:00Z. L2 averaged products are organized by 27-day LRO mapping cycles and day/night local-time bins. L3 hourly products cover local times 19:30 to 05:30, with cumulative/all-hours products also available. The PDS L2 collection metadata gives a slightly different start time (2009-07-05T04:00:00Z); cite the dataset-profile interval as the dataset-level coverage and check individual labels for product intervals.
coordinate_reference_system: L2 products are cylindrical longitude/latitude or polar stereographic. L2 TB fields are channel brightness temperatures, so should not be conflated automatically with bulk/regolith thermodynamic temperature. L3 ST is a derived soil/regolith temperature retrieval from nighttime channels 6–8, fitting measured radiances to a two-component soil-plus-rock model; the rock temperature comes from a thermal model assuming semi-infinite rock with thermal inertia 1000 MKS. No atmosphere variable is listed in these GDR product descriptions.
limitations: L2 uses only nadir-pointing data (activity flag 110), screens thermal brightness temperatures outside 10–450 K and culls excessive-noise observations; uncovered cells remain gaps rather than being interpolated. GDR footprint projection uses LOLA terrain to account for finite footprint and reduce high-latitude aliasing. Dataset profile flags observations immediately after instrument power-on/restart as suspect because pointing may be incorrect or missing. L3 ST/RA are model-based nighttime retrievals with the stated rock assumptions; no retrieval is made where local slope exceeds the equivalent of 80° latitude. A license is not stated on cited pages; L2 output units beyond the stated temperature screening range are not specified on cited pages.

exact_product_name_and_version: PDS dataset version 1.0, archive volume CH1M3_0004 (Level 2). M³ instrument spectral range is reported as 430–3000 nm, constant 10-nm sampling, FWHM <15 nm. The associated _SUP.IMG contains a 1489-nm sphere-photometrically-corrected reflectance image (unitless), a derived-temperature map (temperature units not specified on cited page), and a longest-useful-wavelength Level 1B radiance image (W/(m² µm sr) per pixel; band 84 in Global Mode).

The spacecraft orbit was raised to 200 km on May 19, 2009; exact per-observation ground sampling distance is not specified on cited page and should not be assumed uniform at the nominal value.

Archive volume separates data into 20081118_20090214 and 20090415_20090816 periods, so coverage is not continuous. M³ achieved >95% lunar-surface coverage in Global Mode; coverage is not complete.

download_method: Direct HTTPS PDS Imaging Node volume CH1M3_0004; request only observations intersecting target AOI and keep labels/headers.
authentication_requirements: No authentication requirement is specified on the cited archive page; product-specific license is not specified.
license_or_attribution: A product-specific license is not specified on the cited M³ archive pages. NASA’s science-data policy says CC0 applies by default to data from NASA-led missions unless restrictive terms are marked; that page does not establish that this ISRO-led Chandrayaan-1 archive falls in that category, so do not infer CC0 for this product without checking the file/label terms. PDS supplies this citation: Malaret, E., P. Guasqui, S. McLaughlin, J. Sunshine, S. Besse, R. Clark, and P. Isaacson, CH1-ORB MOON M3 4 L2 REFLECTANCE NEAR-IR SPECTRAL IMAGES V1.0, CH1-ORB-L-M3-4-L2-REFLECTANCE-V1.0, NASA Planetary Data System, 2011.
availability_status: Archived online in PDS Imaging Node volume CH1M3_0004 for Optical Periods 1 and 2, Level 2. It consists of individual observation cubes in the monthly L2 folders, not a ready-made global mosaic. Global Mode covers >95% of the Moon; the M³ archive also includes a limited number of Target Mode observations, which are outside the requested Global Mode subset.
expected_processing_effort: The Level 2 archive already provides resampled, pixel-located, radiometrically calibrated reflectance with thermal removal and photometric correction; basic spectral retrieval can start from the RFL cube and its PDS label/header. Building a global mosaic requires selecting/filtering and registering/mosaicking individual observations. Mineral identification or hydration abundance requires additional spectral-feature analysis and interpretation; archive Level 2 did not apply the optional ground-truth correction.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: This is an observed spectral reflectance product, not a mineral-class or H₂O/OH abundance retrieval. Absorptions in the ~1- and 2-µm regions support mineralogical discrimination; the M³ product SIS specifically discusses 2-µm pyroxene absorptions. A feature in the ~3-µm region is consistent with water molecules and/or hydroxyl-bearing material; NASA/JPL describes the M³ team’s lunar hydration finding as absorption patterns consistent with water and hydroxyl. These are spectral interpretations, not direct output variables or unambiguous abundance measurements.
limitations: Only >95% Global Mode lunar coverage; mission ended before planned later high-resolution observing campaign. Nominal 140-m sampling assumes planned 100-km orbit, while orbit rose to 200 km in May 2009. SIS notes warm/cold instrument states and residual artifacts; cross-Optical-Period weak spectral differences require caution. Statistical polishing can remove weak 1- and 2-µm absorptions; thermal correction can suppress a strong 2-µm absorption. For sufficiently strong 3-µm absorptions, the Level 2 thermal algorithm may derive no temperature and remove no thermal emission; the SIS cautions resulting hydration mapping/abundance is conservative and a lower limit because thermal emission can mask or weaken hydration features. Photometric correction is based on highland terrain and is extrapolated at longer wavelengths; actual products were not ground-truth corrected. Thus apparent features need quality screening and cautious spectral interpretation.

Areoid is defined using the GMM3 (mgm1025) Mars potential model evaluated to degree/order 50. Topography samples represent median observed cell topography; interpolated values are supplied for cells with no observations.

temporal_coverage: PDS archive context dates: 1997-09-15 through 2001-06-30. coordinate_reference_system: IAU 2000 Mars cartographic reference system; planetocentric/areocentric latitude, body-centered, body-fixed rotating frame; positive-east longitude increasing 0°–360° from prime meridian; latitude −90° to +90°. PDS3 catalog explicitly says longitude increases eastward and describes the coordinate system as right-handed.
download_method: Direct PDS Geosciences Node MEGDR directories or Mars ODE; retrieve raster, label/XML and ENVI header for chosen resolution.
authentication_requirements: No login is indicated for archive downloads.
license_or_attribution: A license is not specified on the cited product/archive pages. Cite the migrated bundle DOI 10.17189/1z1b-kv84 (authors listed by PDS: David E. Smith, Greg Neumann, Madison N. Hughes); the legacy PDS3 catalog gives the recommended dataset citation: Smith et al., Mars Global Surveyor Laser Altimeter Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record, NASA PDS, 2003.
availability_status: Archived and online. Maintained PDS4 bundle: https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/mgs/urn-nasa-pds-mgs_mola_topography_derived/ . MEG128 directory: https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/mgs/urn-nasa-pds-mgs_mola_topography_derived/meg128/ . The original PDS3 archive remains available at https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/mgs/mgs-m-mola-5-megdr-l3-v1/mgsl_300x/ .
expected_processing_effort: Feasible to derive slope and terrain ruggedness from the topography rasters; these are not listed as delivered MEGDR variables. For scientifically meaningful derivatives, mosaic matching tiles, use a Mars-aware projected/geodesic or spherical method, handle tile seams and separate polar projections, and account for latitude-dependent ground spacing. Preserve count/coverage masks when possible.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: This is a derived gridded altimetry product, not a formal forward-observation model. The label describes median observed topography per cell and interpolation where cells have no shots; the product includes observation counts. Nearly 600 million observations are represented, subject to stated screening and crossover adjustments.
limitations: Sampling is uneven: the PDS catalog reports only about 55% of equatorial bins contain at least one MOLA shot, with gaps up to 12 km between profiles; empty cells may be interpolated. Thus nominal ppd is grid spacing, not uniform native measurement density or local terrain accuracy. The PDS catalog estimates roughly 40 cm vertical resolution, 300 m along-track sampling, about 30 m absolute long-wavelength radial orbit error, and roughly 400 m spot-location uncertainty at nominal 400 km range. At 128 ppd, polar coverage is in separate map products; use the correct polar projection rather than treating those grids as a seamless cylindrical raster.

provider: NASA National Snow and Ice Data Center Distributed Active Archive Center (NSIDC DAAC)
exact_product_name_and_version: MODIS/Terra Snow Cover Daily L3 Global 500m SIN Grid, Version 61 / Collection 6.1; DOI 10.5067/MODIS/MOD10A1.061
variables_and_units: Daily snow cover (NDSI values 0–100, with cloud/other feature flags) and snow albedo product fields; interpret field-specific codes/scaling using user guide and HDF metadata.
spatial_resolution: 500 m sinusoidal tiles; each granule is 10° x 10°.
temporal_coverage: Daily from 2000-02-24 to present; data latency typically a few days, but may vary.
coordinate_reference_system: Sinusoidal grid; EPSG code not specified on NSIDC product page.
download_method: NSIDC DAAC Data Access Tool/Earthdata Search; spatial, temporal and parameter subsets also via NASA AppEEARS where supported.
authentication_requirements: Free NASA Earthdata Login account required to access/download.
license_or_attribution: Openly shared without restriction under EOSDIS data use/citation guidance; cite DOI 10.5067/MODIS/MOD10A1.061 and NSIDC DAAC.
availability_status: Official NSIDC Version 61 product page is active; not downloaded in this audit.
expected_processing_effort: Moderate: select seasonal/date and AOI, decode HDF-EOS QA/cloud flags, and distinguish NDSI from snow fraction/albedo.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: Daily snow-cover and albedo retrieval derived from MODIS satellite observations; not a direct snow-depth measurement.
limitations: Cloud cover and polar darkness prevent mapping; ephemeral/thin snow can be missed. Antarctic winter observations are especially constrained by polar darkness.

provider: NASA Planetary Data System Geosciences Node; CRISM Science Team/JHU APL
exact_product_name_and_version: MRO CRISM Map-projected Targeted Reduced Data Records (MTRDR), PDS4; current CRISM archive page. Product-specific volumes are MROCR_4001 for listed MTRDR coverage; inspect labels for exact revision.
variables_and_units: Map-projected visible/near-IR spectral image cubes and value-added spectral parameter products; I/F/radiance and summary parameter definitions are product-specific. Spectral signatures support mineral interpretation; derived summary products can have false positives/negatives.
spatial_resolution: Targeted observation-dependent. PDS profile notes CRISM sampling can reach 18 m for full-resolution observations; actual targeted products vary and do not provide uniform global coverage.
temporal_coverage: CRISM observations from 2006 onward; MTRDR volume coverage listed 2006-09-30 to 2012-05-21. Latest additional PDS4 product families have separate volume coverage through 2023 depending on product.
coordinate_reference_system: Product images are map-projected using Martian terrain models; exact projection/coordinate metadata is per PDS label. Not Earth WGS84.
download_method: PDS Geosciences Node CRISM archive or Mars Orbital Data Explorer; select MTRDR observation(s), retain PDS4 labels and quality/summary files.
authentication_requirements: No login requirement specified on the archive access page; direct archive browsing is available.
license_or_attribution: PDS product-specific terms are not stated on the landing page; retain PDS/CRISM citation and metadata. Do not assume a separate open license absent label terms.
availability_status: PDS archive page active; CRISM L observations stopped 2018-02-15 due instrument cooler failure; not downloaded in this audit.
expected_processing_effort: Moderate-to-high: targeted coverage screening, labels, atmospheric/illumination corrections, spectral/summary-parameter QA, then geological interpretation.
observation_model_or_proxy_status: Orbital spectral measurements and derived map-projected records; mineral presence is interpreted from spectral features and is not a direct abundance ground truth.
limitations: Coverage is targeted and patchy; observation resolution varies; PDS notes known calibration/artifact issues and that summary parameters may yield false positives/negatives. No single global mineral raster.
source_basis: PHASE1_PLANNED_CATALOG_PRESERVED_NOT_PROOF_OF_ACQUISITION
